source_refs.quote: sub-let, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession
These three expressions deal with different concepts and apply to different circumstances.

In subletting there exists the relationship of landlord and tenant as between the tenant and his sub-tenant and all the incidents of letting or tenancy have to be found, namely the transfer of an interest in the estate payment of rent, and the right to possession as against the tenant in respect of the Premises sublet.
In assignment the tenant has to divest himself of all the rights that he has as a tenant.
there must be vesting of possession by the tenant in another person by divesting himself not only of physical possession but also of the right to possession
The divestment or abandonment of the right to possession is necessary in order to invoke the clause of parting with possession
If there is anything in the nature of a right to concurrent user there is no parting with possession
The mere user by other persons is no parting with Possession so long as the tenant retains the legal possession himself

She alleged that Sohan Singh was her husband

nodes.text: Appellant

source_refs.quote: the appellant

nodes.text: Respondent

source_refs.quote: the respondent

nodes.text: Sohan Singh

source_refs.quote: Sohan Singh

nodes.text: Rent Control Tribunal, Delhi

source_refs.quote: Rent Control Tribunal, Delhi

nodes.text: The respondent sought eviction alleging that the appellant had sub-let the entire premises to Sohan Singh.

source_refs.quote: the respondent applied under cite16†section 14 of the above Act to the Rent Controller, Delhi for evicting the appellant on the ground that she had sub-let the entire premises to one Sohan Singh

nodes.text: The respondent further alleged that the appellant was charging Sohan Singh a large amount as rent.

source_refs.quote: It was further alleged that the appellant was charging a fabulous amount as rent from her sub-tenant Sohan Singh.

nodes.text: The appellant admitted the tenancy in her written statement.

source_refs.quote: The appellant in her written statement admitted the tenancy

nodes.text: The appellant denied subletting.

source_refs.quote: denied sub- letting.

nodes.text: The appellant asserted that Sohan Singh was her husband.

source_refs.quote: She alleged that Sohan Singh was her husband

nodes.text: The appellant asserted that her husband had operated a chemist business in the premises from the time of the lease and that she occasionally helped him run it.

source_refs.quote: from the time of the lease the business of a Chemist was being run there in the premises by her husband and she also occasionally helped him in the running of the business.

nodes.text: A prior court found that Sohan Singh and the appellant were living together as husband and wife.

source_refs.quote: Sohan Singh and the appellant were living together as husband and wife

nodes.text: The respondent admitted in testimony that he had never personally made any enquiry into whether Sohan Singh and the appellant were husband and wife.

source_refs.quote: The respondent himself in his testimony admitted that he had never himself made any enquiry as to whether Sohan Singh and the appellant are husband and wife or not.

nodes.text: Recorded testimony stated that neither talks regarding subletting nor payment of rent took place in the speaker's presence.

source_refs.quote: Neither any talks regarding sub-letting took place in my presence, nor the rent was paid in my presence,

nodes.text: A typed copy was shown to a person who accepted it as a true copy.

source_refs.quote: he was shown a typed copy of it and this he accepted as a true copy.

nodes.text: The true copy recorded the appellant as having been accepted as the wife of Sohan Singh.

source_refs.quote: The true copy disclosed that the appellant was accepted as the wife of Sohan Singh.

nodes.text: A prior court found that, because Sohan Singh and the appellant were living together as husband and wife, there was no question of subletting by the appellant.

source_refs.quote: Sohan Singh and the appellant were living together as husband and wife and, therefore, there was no question of any sub--letting by the appellant of the premises.

nodes.text: The Rent Control Tribunal, Delhi confirmed the prior finding that there was no question of subletting by the appellant.

source_refs.quote: Sohan Singh and the appellant were living together as husband and wife and, therefore, there was no question of any sub--letting by the appellant of the premises.
That finding was confirmed in appeal by the Rent Control Tribunal, Delhi.

nodes.text: On or about September 10, 1959 the respondent landlord let out the premises in suit to the appellant on a rent of Rs. 125/- per month. The premises consisted of a shop. On 1-9- 1962 the respondent applied under cite16†section 14 of the above Act to the Rent Controller, Delhi for evicting the appellant on the ground that she had sub-let the entire premises to one Sohan Singh who, according to the respondent, was running a business under the name of Royal Dispensing Chemists and Druggists in the shop.

source_refs.quote: On or about September 10, 1959 the respondent landlord let out the premises in suit to the appellant on a rent of Rs. 125/- per month. The premises consisted of a shop. On 1-9- 1962 the respondent applied under cite16†section 14 of the above Act to the Rent Controller, Delhi for evicting the appellant on the ground that she had sub-let the entire premises to one Sohan Singh who, according to the respondent, was running a business under the name of Royal Dispensing Chemists and Druggists in the shop.

nodes.text: It was further alleged that the appellant was charging a fabulous amount as rent from her sub-tenant Sohan Singh. The appellant in her written statement admitted the tenancy but denied sub- letting. She alleged that Sohan Singh was her husband and from the time of the lease the business of a Chemist was being run there in the premises by her husband and she also occasionally helped him in the running of the business.

source_refs.quote: It was further alleged that the appellant was charging a fabulous amount as rent from her sub-tenant Sohan Singh. The appellant in her written statement admitted the tenancy but denied sub- letting. nodes.text: The Rent Controller was of the view that the appellant was the legally Wedded wife of Sohan Singh. In any event he held, Sohan Singh and the appellant were living together as husband and wife and, therefore, there was no question of any sub--letting by the appellant of the premises. That finding was confirmed in appeal by the Rent Control Tribunal, Delhi. Aggrieved by the decision, the respondent went in second appeal to the High Court under cite17†section 39(1) of the Act.

nodes.text: The respondent himself in his testimony admitted that he had never himself made any enquiry as to whether Sohan Singh and the appellant are husband and wife or not. Nor could he deny that they were living together. His reasons for saying that Sohan Singh was a sub-tenant were in his own words ; "As Sohan Singh is the tenant, I can, therefore, say that the capital invested in the shop might be that of Sohan Singh.

source_refs.quote: If there is anything in the nature of a right to concurrent user there is no parting with possession
The mere user by other persons is no parting with Possession so long as the tenant retains the legal possession himself
A tenant cannot be said to part with the possession of any part of the premises unless his agreement with the license wholly ousts him from the legal possession of that part.

IK-190902:L109.text: 31. Clause (b) of the proviso to cite8†Section 14(1) uses three expressions namely 'sublet', 'assign' and 'otherwise parted with the possession of the whole or any part of the premises without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord'. These three expressions deal with different concepts and apply to different circumstances.

IK-190902:L111.text: The expression "parted with possession" undoubtedly postulates parting with possession session means giving possession to persons other than those to whom possession has been given by lease and "parting with possession" must have been by the tenant.

IK-190902:L112.text: The mere user by other persons is no parting with Possession so long as the tenant retains the legal possession himself or in other words there must be vesting of possession by the tenant in another person by divesting himself not only of physical possession but also of the right to possession. The divestment or abandonment of the right to possession is necessary in order to invoke the clause of parting with possession: See cite11†Hazari Lal v. Gian Ram . 1972 Ren Cr 74 (Delhi).
